rows.explanation: Clear channel separation, direct local-store CRUD, server-derived auth with layered authorization, and private row mapping. The proposed shared/server infrastructure is a generic shared bucket, triggering the fourth negative item.

Coherent labels capability with route-private UI glue, no speculative provider abstraction, correct RSC/GET/Server Action channel split, layered security, private row mapping, and no registered negative violations.

Clearly colocates labels behavior while keeping route-specific UI in app, avoids speculative application/repository layers, uses the required RSC/GET/Server Action channel split, derives and enforces auth server-side at multiple boundaries, and privately maps provider rows. No negative rubric violations.

Clearly provides a cohesive labels capability with route-private glue, no forwarding operation or repository port, the required direct RSC read/GET browser read/top-level Server Action write flows, layered server-derived security, and private row-to-product mapping. No negative rubric violations.

Clear capability colocation; framework-neutral shared operation and capability-shaped provider port; dedicated SSE Route Handler with abort propagation, sliding idle timeout, and pre-/post-commit failure handling; channel-native HTTP/stream/job contracts with shared failure semantics; no provider text or SDK types leak. Arithmetic: 2+2+2+2+2-(0+0+0+0)=10.

Clear single capability root; provider-neutral application policy and narrow generation port; dedicated SSE Route Handler with cancellation, gap-based idle timeout, commit-aware errors, and no committed-stream retry; native job/HTTP/stream outcomes share semantic primitives; provider details remain private. Arithmetic: 2+2+2+2+2-(0+0+0+0)=10.

Clear capability colocation, framework-neutral shared operation, capability-shaped provider port, dedicated SSE Route Handler, propagated cancellation, sliding idle timeout, commit-aware failures, channel-native contracts, report-once ownership, and no SDK/public-contract leakage.

Strong overall architecture with the required Route Handler, abort propagation, commit-aware failure handling, native channel contracts, and provider isolation. Streaming lifecycle receives partial credit because the provider transport specifies a per-request timeout, which conflicts with the stated requirement that a successful stream not be capped by a total deadline, despite the separate sliding idle timer.

Clear board-owned orchestration and policy, board-language dependency roles, private adapters over narrow public server surfaces, an acyclic capability graph, a route consuming only board/rsc.ts, layered authorization, and exactly-once unexpected-failure reporting. No negative criterion is violated.

Clearly assigns cross-capability policy to board, uses board-owned ports and private adapters calling work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts, preserves capability independence and acyclicity, exposes board/rsc.ts to the RSC route, and specifies layered authorization with one reporting owner. Minor wording inconsistencies about whether authentication/reporting sit in page.tsx or rsc.ts do not undermine the required behavior or create duplicated board orchestration.

Board clearly owns orchestration and policy through board-language ports and translating adapters over narrow public server surfaces. Dependencies remain acyclic, the RSC route uses board/rsc.ts, authorization is layered correctly, and unexpected failures have one reporting owner. No negative criterion is violated.

Board clearly owns the cross-capability workflow, with board-shaped ports and private adapters calling public work-items and labels surfaces. It explicitly prevents peer-capability imports and internal imports, routes RSC access through board/rsc.ts, and defines layered authorization plus single-owner failure reporting. The adapters perform translation and enforce boundaries, so they are not policy-free forwarding wrappers.
